headline: Google Kills Custom Search API on Jan 1, 2027
summary: Developers relying on Google's Custom Search API will need to find alternatives as the service is slated for shutdown on January 1, 2027.
details: Google has announced the discontinuation of its Custom Search API, effective January 1, 2027. This move impacts developers and websites that integrate Google's search capabilities directly into their platforms.

The Custom Search API allowed programmatic access to Google Search results, enabling custom search experiences for specific websites or collections of sites. It provided a flexible way for developers to leverage Google's powerful search engine.

While Google has not yet provided specific reasons for the shutdown, such decisions often reflect a shift in product strategy or resource allocation. Developers are advised to begin exploring alternative solutions for their search needs.

Potential alternatives include building custom search solutions using open-source search engines or integrating with other third-party search providers. This transition period offers ample time for migration planning and implementation.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Lingbot-map: 3D foundation model reconstructs scenes from streaming data]]
headline: Lingbot-map: 3D foundation model reconstructs scenes from streaming data
summary: Lingbot-map is a PyTorch-based 3D foundation model that reconstructs scenes from streaming data, offering interactive visualization and offline rendering capabilities for complex environments.
details: Lingbot-map is a new 3D foundation model designed to reconstruct complex scenes directly from streaming data. Built on PyTorch, it offers both interactive 3D visualization and a robust offline rendering pipeline.

The model recommends PyTorch 2.8.0 with NVIDIA Kaolin for optimal performance, leveraging FlashInfer for efficient streaming inference. FlashInfer is a pure-Python package that JIT-compiles CUDA kernels, ensuring broad compatibility across CUDA/PyTorch versions.

For extended sequences, Lingbot-map employs a keyframe interval strategy to reduce KV cache memory, maintaining performance beyond 320 frames. This approach prevents performance degradation and is crucial for processing long video inputs effectively.

Users can explore interactive 3D visualizations via a local browser-based viser viewer, or utilize the offline rendering pipeline for headless point-cloud flythrough MP4 generation. This allows for processing sequences too long for real-time interaction.

The model integrates sky masking, using an ONNX sky segmentation model to filter out sky points, enhancing visualization quality for outdoor scenes. Sky masks are automatically downloaded and cached for subsequent runs.

To address out-of-memory issues, users can lower camera refinement steps or refer to an optimized implementation for GPUs with limited VRAM. The system also supports a windowed mode for handling pose collapse in very long inference ranges.
caption:
Reconstruct entire 3D scenes in real-time from streaming data. Lingbot-map is a new foundation model for dynamic environment mapping.
